title: Normalized slice scalar adjunction and product Hom chain isomorphism
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe, $\varphi:R\to S$ a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings, $E=S\otimes_R-$ the sheafification of sectionwise scalar extension and $U$ restriction of scalars, both applied termwise to unbounded cochain complexes [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Write $T(A)=S\otimes_R A$ for the underlying $R$-linear sheaf tensor, termwise. Write $H_R(P,J)=\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(P,J)$ and $H_S(K,N)=\mathcal Hom_S^\bullet(K,N)$ for the actual product Hom complexes [def-pur-hom-complex]; their local degree-$n$ sections have coordinates $f^i:P^i|_W\to J^{i+n}|_W$ on $\mathcal C/W$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. All pure tensors below mean their images under the tensor sheafification units [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], and evaluation means the actual product projection followed by evaluation at the identity object of the slice.
For every object $W$, every $R|_W$-module sheaf $M$ and $S|_W$-module sheaf $L$, the assignments
$$g\longmapsto(x\mapsto g(1\otimes x)),\qquad h\longmapsto(s\otimes x\mapsto s h(x))$$
are mutually inverse additive bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_{S|_W}(S|_W\otimes_{R|_W}M,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{R|_W}(M,UL)$, compatible with further slice restriction and pre- and postcomposition. There is a natural chain isomorphism $\nu_A:T(A)\xrightarrow{\sim}UEA$ sending $s\otimes x$ to $s\otimes x$. For arbitrary $R$-complex $P$ and $S$-complex $N$ there is a natural $R$-linear chain isomorphism
$$\theta_{P,N}:U H_S(EP,N)\xrightarrow{\sim} H_R(P,UN),\qquad (\theta(g))^i(p)=g^i(1\otimes p),$$
whose inverse in degree $n$ sends a local family $(h^i)_i$ to the family of $S|_W$-linear sheaf maps $s\otimes p\mapsto s h^i(p)$. Here $d(f)^i=d_J f^i-(-1)^n f^{i+1}d_P$, and the asserted isomorphism commutes with this differential. Naturality of $\theta$ is contravariant in $P$ and covariant in $N$. No flatness, boundedness, finite-support, K-injectivity, or preservation of infinite products by $E$ is assumed.

proof.text: Use the already proved canonical data underlying the strict scalar-Hom identification, with its canonical extension E and natural chain isomorphisms nu and theta. Retain their forward normalization and naturality. For theta inverse, put g=theta inverse(f). The forward formula gives f(x)=g(1 tensor x). S-linearity of the actual Hom coordinate and s tensor x=s(1 tensor x) then give g(s tensor x)=s f(x).

Reuse the already proved private ordinary scalar-extension functor, its additivity proof, the module/presheaf/sheaf scalar Hom equivalence and the ordinary adjunction from StrictScalarHomChain, imported privately with import all. Their objectwise normalization is evaluation at one tensor x. Transport the adjunction to any prescribed Extension using its object and map equalities. Evaluation on generators proves the forward formula and additivity; linearity at s(1 tensor x) and the equivalence inverse law prove the inverse formula. Apply this construction also to each slice.

For a continuous cocontinuous functor F between sites with independent universes, transpose the restricted global module sheafification unit through the local sheafification adjunction. The defining inverse law says that the local unit followed by this comparison is the restricted global unit. The latter is locally injective and locally surjective by cocontinuity. Cancel the locally bijective local unit; a locally bijective morphism of module sheaves is an isomorphism. This repeats the argument of the former small-site slice comparison directly at the universes required here.

The scalar-extension presheaf restricted along F is canonically isomorphic to the scalar-extension presheaf of the restricted module: on each section it is the identity on the tensor product; the tensor restriction formula checks naturality. Sheafify this isomorphism and compose with the preceding comparison to obtain the inverse-direction scalar comparison. Naturality of the sheafification unit and its transpose prove that this comparison preserves every pure tensor. Equality on pure tensors gives naturality in the module. Apply to Over.forget W and Over.map a (both continuous and cocontinuous), invert the comparisons, using the canonical extension directly. The resulting natural isomorphisms and pure formulas are exactly overIso/over_pure and furtherIso/further_pure. Assemble these with the ordinary adjunctions and the chain data from the first step.

The item is unsplit with an empty proof in live and side-live, has no repair note, and neither it nor any node it cites is on the route-pivot drop list. Its statement, stmt_deps, source and blueprint from are unchanged from live. I read all 7 steps against the statements of every cited node and against Stacks sites-modules 03CZ (l.933, proof via the presheaf tensor plus the sheaf property), 03CY, 03DH and 04IX, and sites-cohomology 0A8X (l.8571; the sign d(f)^p=d^{p+n}f^p-(-1)^n f^{p+1}d matches def-pur-hom-complex). Step 1: j_W is continuous and cocontinuous (the same arrows composed to W generate the sieve), and the comparison from lem-weil-pbc-slice-module-sheafification is the transpose of the restricted unit, so 1⊗x goes to 1⊗x. Step 2: E_W is additive; s·h(x) is balanced because s·h(rx)=s·φ(r)h(x); the tensor and module-sheafification universal properties give the map, and its adjunct is h, so it is the inverse of the bijection stated by the ordinary-adjunction node. Steps 3–7 are elementary and I recomputed each: R(W)-linearity; naturality b(g(1⊗a x)); ν as one abelian sheafification with a unique R-action; θ as a coordinatewise product, so E is never applied to a product; the differential θ(dg)^i(p)=d_N g^i(1⊗p)-(-1)^n g^{i+1}(1⊗d_P p); and two-variable naturality. Every argument from the parent's base steps 1–5 and the ν/θ part of step 10 is covered. Edge cases checked: S=0, R=S, Z→F_2, unbounded constant complexes, characteristic 2. The duplicate search found no existing node stating the item; the siblings cite it. I accept the two tool_uses, both generic other-unit tools: the slice sheafification comparison and the ordinary scalar adjunction. Advisory only: step 4 could also cite lem-weil-pbc-extension-tensor-comparison and step 1 could cite lem-sfb-localized-site-tensor-restriction; mathlib_searches has duplicate entries. No changes.
